newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil court in South awaits CVRD appeal.
newsitem.headline: Brazil court in South awaits CVRD appeal.

text.p: A Brazilian federal court in the southern state of Rio Grande do Sul was still awaiting a government appeal against an injunction blocking the sale of Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), a spokeswoman said.
"We have not received anything yet," said the spokeswoman for the Regional Federal Tribunal in the state capital Porto Allegre.

The Rio Grande do Sul injunction was the last of three blocking the start of Latin America's largest privatization to date after a high court judge Monday night revoked a host of previous court orders.

Justice officials in Rio de Janeiro said there were rumors that two new injunctions had been granted in the northeastern state of Maranhao Tuesday morning, but court officials in the state could not confirm the reports.
Monday night's high court ruling named a Rio tribunal as responsible for considering all new CVRD cases.

But the rumored court cases in Maranhao were supposedly so-called "public civil actions" as opposed to "popular actions". The high court decision only referred to popular actions, a spokeswoman for the Rio judicial authorities said.
It was therefore not immediately clear whether the auction could or would go ahead as soon as government lawyers managed to quash the Rio Grande do Sul injunction.
Earlier, the Rio Regional Federal Tribunal overturned two injunctions that had been issued in the city.
Delayed since April 29, the auction of up to 45 percent of CVRD's voting stock was tentatively rescheduled for Tuesday.
The Rio stock exchange where it was due to take place said it was ready at any time to hold the auction once all legal obstacles were removed.
